description: Realtime Sync Perf — Workstream 3 (Server Replay Buffer + Client lastSeenSeq Handshake): eliminate the HTTP re-fetch fallback on every Socket.IO reconnect by adding a per-daemon in-memory ring buffer (1024 entries) plus a currentSeq tracker on the server, and a per-daemon lastSeenUpdateSeqByMachineId MMKV-persisted state plus monotonic setter on the client. Reconnects with a stored lastSeenSeq replay silently from the buffer; cap-overflow or daemon-restart emit a distinct replay-overflow event that triggers an HTTP fallback. Lands as a single commit on main.

planReviewContext.description: Persistence hook is too narrow and unsafe for paths that don't reach apply* sinks. new-session (sync.ts ~1765-1799) and delete-session call sessionsSync.invalidate() (fire-and-forget), NOT applySessions / applyMachines / applyProfile. Persisting lastSeenUpdateSeq before the async fetch completes can permanently skip the update on next reconnect. Fix: persist exactly once per successfully handled update (after the entire handleUpdate body succeeds and at a known-safe point), not only after the listed apply* sites; and for events that defer to invalidate(), persist only after the invalidate resolves successfully.
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Move the persist call to a single location at the successful tail of handleUpdate. For new-session / delete-session paths that defer to sessionsSync.invalidate(), either await the invalidate (use invalidateAndAwait()) before persisting OR persist inside a .then() callback on the existing invalidate path. Document the constraint in a comment.

planReviewContext.description: The 'first-connect HTTP refresh' decision is parked in Open Questions but is load-bearing for correctness (without it, a fresh user with no stored seq sees nothing until something happens). Move from Open Questions to a committed design decision in the Approach section.
planReviewContext.suggestedFix: Same fix as F-002. Commit the design: onReconnected calls invalidate iff storage slot is undefined.

userStories.title: Server ring buffer + currentSeq tracker in EventRouter
userStories.description: As a happy-server daemon, I want to retain the last 1024 emitted update events (plus a parallel currentSeq integer) so a reconnecting client can resume from a known lastSeenSeq without an HTTP re-fetch. Flat buffer + single currentSeq is sound because each daemon serves exactly one operator.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/happy-server/sources/app/events/eventRouter.ts adds module-scoped state: a flat replayBuffer: BufferedUpdate[] (BufferedUpdate = { payload, recipientFilter, createdAt }) AND a module-scoped let currentSeq = 0 integer. Neither is keyed by userId.

appendToReplayBuffer(payload, recipientFilter) is invoked inside EventRouterSink.emitUpdate strictly after seq allocation; pushes to the array with createdAt = Date.now(), drops the oldest element when length > 1024, and writes currentSeq = payload.seq in lockstep.

When emitUpdate is called without an explicit recipientFilter, the same default applied at the live publish path ({ type: 'all-user-authenticated-connections' }) is stored in the buffer entry so replay matches the original broadcast.

getReplayForConnection(lastSeenSeq, connection) returns { events: UpdatePayload[]; overflow: boolean; currentSeq: number } with overflow logic: (currentSeq > 0 && lastSeenSeq > currentSeq) OR (buffer non-empty && lastSeenSeq < replayBuffer[0].payload.seq). No-op when currentSeq === 0; when lastSeenSeq >= currentSeq and buffer empty; or when lastSeenSeq >= replayBuffer[0].payload.seq and lastSeenSeq <= currentSeq (resume-in-window).
Partial replay iterates buffered entries and includes a payload only when entry.payload.seq > lastSeenSeq AND doesFilterMatchConnection(entry.recipientFilter, connection) returns true.

Private helper doesFilterMatchConnection(filter, connection) inside EventRouterSink mirrors getRoomsForFilter exactly: all-user-authenticated-connections -> always true; user-scoped-only -> only user-scoped connections; all-interested-in-session -> user-scoped OR (session-scoped with matching sessionId); machine-scoped-only -> user-scoped OR (machine-scoped with matching machineId). Cross-reference comments at both helper sites.
Cap-only retention at 1024 entries (no age-eviction).
Inline comment at append site explains the allocateUserSeq-before-emitUpdate ordering invariant.
Inline comment at module-scoped declarations documents the flat-buffer rationale (one-user-per-daemon deployment invariant) and the escape hatches if the invariant is relaxed.

Unit test (eventRouter.test.ts): emit 10 events with default filter; reconnect a user-scoped connection with lastSeenSeq=5 -> replay returns events 6..10 in ascending seq order; other previously-attached connections do NOT receive the replay events.
Unit test: emit 2000 events -> buffer length is exactly 1024 and oldest entry seq is 977.
Unit test: buffer oldest seq 977, lastSeenSeq=0 -> overflow=true with currentSeq=2000 and no event payloads on the overflow path.

Unit test (recipientFilter matrix): emit four events with each of the four RecipientFilter types; reconnect against five connection shapes (user-scoped; session-scoped for s1; session-scoped for unrelated session; machine-scoped for m1; machine-scoped for unrelated machine) -> each returns exactly the matching subset per the lockstep mapping.

userStories.title: Client handleUpdate persistence + replay-overflow handler + onReconnected gating
userStories.description: As happy-app, I want handleUpdate to persist the last applied seq safely across both synchronous-apply and invalidate-deferred branches, install a replay-overflow handler that falls back to HTTP, and stop unconditionally calling sessionsSync.invalidate() on reconnect.
acceptanceCriteria: In packages/happy-app/sources/sync/sync.ts, handleUpdate(update, isReplay, sourceMachineId) persists lastSeenUpdateSeqByMachineId[sourceMachineId] = updateData.seq at the successful tail, gated on sourceMachineId && typeof updateData.seq === 'number'.
Synchronous-apply branches (update-session, update-account, update-machine, delete-machine, and new-message apply path against a known session) persist directly at the tail.

Invalidate-deferred branches (new-session, delete-session) replace the fire-and-forget sessionsSync.invalidate() with sessionsSync.invalidateAndAwait(); capture the returned promise locally and chain the tail-persist via deferredInvalidate.then(() => storage.getState().setLastSeenUpdateSeq(sourceMachineId, updateData.seq)).

The new-message early-return-on-missing-session path chains the persist inside the existing .finally(...) after the pending-replay loop and returns without falling through to the tail. When isReplay === true on that path, the existing log+drop behavior stays and no persist runs.
Persistence is skipped on safeParse validation-error early return (no setter call).
Replayed events (isReplay === true) that reach the successful tail DO persist.
Inline comment at the tail-persist site explains why persist must run after the branch effects have committed.

apiSocket.onMessage('replay-overflow', (data, machineId) => …) handler is registered near the existing onMessage('update', ...) registration. Handler calls this.sessionsSync.invalidateAndAwait(); on resolve, if typeof data?.currentSeq === 'number', calls storage.getState().setLastSeenUpdateSeq(machineId, data.currentSeq). On rejection the setter is NOT called.

apiSocket.onReconnected((machineId) => …) body is rewritten: always call this.machinesSync.invalidate(); then read storage.getState().lastSeenUpdateSeqByMachineId[machineId] — if undefined, call this.sessionsSync.invalidate() (first-connect path); if a finite number, do NOT call sessionsSync.invalidate() (resume path).
Inline comment in onReconnected references the WS3 gating decision.

Unit test (synchronous-apply + new-session combined per F-012): invoke Sync.handleUpdate 3 times with seqs 1, 2, 3 and sourceMachineId='mA' covering update-session against a known session AND at least one new-session event; after each call, storage.getState().lastSeenUpdateSeqByMachineId['mA'] equals the latest seq once the relevant promise resolves.

Unit test (invalidate-deferred branch): invoke handleUpdate with a new-session event and sessionsSync.invalidateAndAwait stubbed to return a pending promise; assert setter NOT called yet. After resolving the promise, assert setter called with correct seq.
Unit test (validation failure): invoke handleUpdate with a payload that fails safeParse; assert setter is NOT called.

Unit test (replay-overflow handler): receiving the event with { replayOverflow: true, currentSeq: 42 } calls sessionsSync.invalidateAndAwait; on resolve, setter is called with 42. On rejection (per F-013), setter is NOT called.

Unit test (onReconnected first-connect branch): when lastSeenUpdateSeqByMachineId[machineId] is undefined, sessionsSync.invalidate is invoked exactly once AND machinesSync.invalidate is invoked exactly once.

Unit test (onReconnected resume branch): when lastSeenUpdateSeqByMachineId[machineId] is a finite number (seed storage with e.g. 42), sessionsSync.invalidate is NOT invoked (spy call count 0); machinesSync.invalidate is still invoked exactly once.

userStories.title: Documentation updates
userStories.description: As a future contributor or reviewer, I want the WS3 design, invariants, and accepted v1 trade-offs documented in the project living docs.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/happy-server/CLAUDE.md gains a 'Ring buffer' subsection documenting: flat BufferedUpdate[] + let currentSeq shape (NOT keyed by userId); cap-only retention at 1024; single-process / cross-cluster Redis deferred; allocateUserSeq-before-emitUpdate ordering invariant; one-user-per-daemon deployment invariant with escape-hatch note (re-introduce userId-keying + per-account allocateUserSeq if invariant is relaxed). Cross-reference packages/happy-cli/src/daemon/dualListenerBinding.ts and sources/storage/seq.ts.

packages/happy-app/CLAUDE.md gains a note documenting: lastSeenUpdateSeqByMachineId is per-daemon and tracks updateData.seq (account-global per daemon), not session.seq; the onReconnected gating change (invalidate iff stored seq is undefined; resume reconnects rely on server replay; cap-overflow triggers replay-overflow handler); the accepted per-event MMKV write rate as a v1 trade-off (F-008) with the monotonic setter no-op-on-regressing guard as the mitigation; and the asymmetric design (client IS per-machine because it talks to many daemons; server is NOT per-user because each daemon serves only its single owner).
plans/realtime-sync-perf.md §Workstream 3 gains a footer line 'Status: implemented YYYY-MM-DD in commit <sha>' with cross-references to touched files.
Typecheck passes (docs only — no code changes).
